runs.reason:
I lean **YES**, narrowly. The main uncertainty is whether HP clears the EPS threshold, not whether it reports on November 24.

**Base rate.** HP’s fiscal Q4 non-GAAP diluted net EPS cleared $0.75 in all four years from FY2022 through FY2025. But this year’s threshold is one cent above HP’s own guidance midpoint, and only one of those four quarters beat its midpoint by at least a cent. That makes the raw 4-for-4 record a poor guide to this year’s result. ([investor.hp.com](https://investor.hp.com/news-events/news/news-details/2022/HP-Inc.-Reports-Fiscal-2022-Full-Year-and-Fourth-Quarter-Results-Announces-Dividend-Increase-and-Future-Ready-Transformation/default.aspx))

**What moves this case.** On August 26, HP gave Q4 non-GAAP diluted net EPS guidance of $0.69–$0.79, including an estimated $0.08 tariff-refund benefit. The $0.74 midpoint weighs against YES, but HP beat its guidance midpoint in each of the first three quarters of FY2026, which pushes the other way. Its August 27 filing disclosed that it had already received $91 million in tariff refunds after July 31. That makes the refund assumption more credible; it is not a reason to add another $0.08 to guidance. Gartner’s October 12 estimate that HP’s calendar-Q3 PC shipments fell 30.9% year over year is a downside signal, though that period only partly overlaps HP’s fiscal Q4 and unit shipments do not directly measure earnings. ([investor.hp.com](https://investor.hp.com/news-events/news/news-details/2026/HP-Inc--Reports-Fiscal-2026-First-Quarter-Results/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))

**Timing risk.** HP announced on November 3 that it would review results at 5:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 24. I put the chance of no qualifying release on that date at about 1%; a release on a different date would resolve NO regardless of EPS. ([investor.hp.com](https://investor.hp.com/news-events/news/news-details/2026/HP-Inc--to-Announce-Fourth-Quarter-Fiscal-2026-Earnings-on-November-24-2026-and-to-Attend-Upcoming-Investor-Conferences/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))

While HP has consistently exceeded guidance throughout fiscal 2026, the threshold of $0.75 is positioned one cent above both the company's guidance midpoint ($0.74) and the Zacks Consensus Estimate ($0.74). If memory and storage cost inflation compressed Personal Systems margins more severely than anticipated during the October quarter, or if any portion of the projected $0.08 per share tariff refund benefit slipped past the October 31 fiscal year-end cutoff, non-GAAP EPS could easily land at $0.74 or below. (The chance that HP fails to publish its results on November 24, 2026, is negligible—around 1%—given the formal November 3 schedule announcement and the smooth leadership transition announcement on November 4 appointing Emma Walmsley as CEO effective January 2027.)

Balancing HP's strong track record of beating its quarterly guidance midpoints in FY26 against the fact that $0.75 sits above the $0.74 guidance midpoint and Zacks consensus amid known Q4 margin headwinds, a YES outcome is slightly favored.
